hero.title: Multiphysics
hero.subtitle: Open, modular simulation of coupled physical processes
hero.lede: A research project aimed at developing a free and open-source computational environment in which materials, machines, process configurations, physical models, numerical methods, calculation engines and post-processing tools can evolve independently and be recombined as needed.
hero.status: Current academic reference process: flash-butt welding. Current implementation: an evolving research platform, not a finished industrial product.

diagram.ariaLabel: Materials, machines and process feed physics and numerical methods, then calculation engines and post-processing.

vision.title: A reusable FOSS process-simulation platform
vision.body: Multiphysics explores how an integrated process-simulation environment can be developed with a FOSS architecture, open scientific access and explicit separation between physical models, numerical methods and software implementations. The software is the long-term engineering artifact; modelling, numerical, experimental and validation problems encountered along the way are expected to generate independent scientific contributions and publications.

foss.definition: Free and Open Source Software: software distributed under licences that grant freedoms to use, study, modify and redistribute the software. Here, “free” refers primarily to those freedoms, not necessarily to zero price.

simulation.definition: A computational representation of selected physical behaviour under explicit models, assumptions and numerical approximations; it is not a claim of exact reproduction of the real process.

access.definition: Open access means that scientific material can be publicly read or consulted. It does not, by itself, grant unrestricted reuse; reuse of software, data, text or figures depends on the applicable licence and rights.

platform.definition: A modular research and software environment in which models, numerical methods, calculation engines, data and workflows can be combined. It does not mean a commercial marketplace or necessarily a hosted online service.

vision.pageDescription: Long-term vision for the Multiphysics open modular research platform.

reference.title: Why flash-butt welding?
reference.body: Flash-butt welding is the first process used to develop and stress the architecture, not the final scope of the platform. It combines electrical contact, resistance heating, flashing, heat transfer, moving boundaries, material loss, mechanical deformation, upsetting and metallurgical evolution in a single process family.
reference.note: The choice also builds on previous research from 2018, providing an established scientific starting point. The collaborators initially approached were contacted because their publications and academic work relate directly to the scientific questions addressed here. As the project evolves, additional researchers may be invited on the same basis, using relevant academic production as a starting point for focused, asynchronous scientific collaboration. Components developed here are intended to be reusable or adaptable where their governing assumptions remain valid.

architecture.title: Independent scientific and computational axes
architecture.intro: The architecture deliberately keeps problem definition, physical modelling, numerical discretisation, calculation engines and post-processing distinct.

materials.title: DP600 is the current dataset, not a platform restriction
materials.body: The current material database is being assembled around DP600 steel. Collaborators may provide sufficiently documented experimental data for other metallic materials; those datasets can motivate new material entries and new validation cases.

current.title: Consolidating the one-dimensional model
current.principle: Correct and traceable models before larger models.
current.body: The present priority is methodological correctness and experimental traceability before computational scale. Work is concentrated on consolidating the 1D numerical evidence, machine parametrisation, process configuration, material-property data, and the experimental basis required before flashing/upsetting modelling, calibration and validation can advance.

collaborate.title: The current bottleneck is data
collaborate.body: Software development is not a prerequisite for collaboration. The immediate need is experimentally grounded information capable of constraining, calibrating and validating the models.
collaborate.rights: Data ownership, redistribution rights and publication permissions are treated independently. Scientific use does not automatically imply permission to publish raw data.
collaborate.credit: Contributions may lead to formal project participation and, where the scientific contribution justifies it, co-authorship of resulting publications.
collaborate.questionsIntro: Researchers have already been approached with questions derived from their published work. The examples below are anonymized and illustrate the type of scientific exchange sought by the project.

questions.thermalCycles: Can measured welding thermal cycles be shared as numerical time–temperature series rather than only as plotted figures?
questions.processHistories: Can representative process schedules, stage boundaries, electrical signals, displacement or burn-off histories be made available in processed, anonymized or stage-averaged form?
questions.validationObservables: Which observables are most reliable for validating a reduced flash-butt-welding model when direct interface measurements are unavailable?
questions.materialTransfer: Which material-state variables and phase-transformation data should a reusable material library prioritize, and how should material properties be separated from process-specific calibration?

collaborate.confidentialityBody: Some relevant datasets may be owned by companies, protected by contractual confidentiality, or constitute industrially sensitive information and therefore cannot be disclosed. No researcher is expected to violate those obligations, and sharing raw proprietary data is not a prerequisite for contributing.
collaborate.criticalFeedback: When data cannot be released, researchers who choose to engage are explicitly asked for a critical technical assessment instead. Comments on questionable assumptions, missing physics, unrealistic machine or process inputs, unsuitable validation observables, or relevant literature may be sent directly to the project lead. This kind of feedback is treated as a substantive scientific contribution and is highly valued.

footer.statement: This website presents the publishable scientific state of the Multiphysics project. It does not expose private correspondence, internal researcher profiles or unpublished collaborative material.
